subject: Renewal proposal — Support tier uplift & SLO addendum for AtlasCare
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Michael Tan <mtan@atlascare.io>, Procurement <procure@atlascare.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal proposal — Support tier uplift & SLO addendum for AtlasCare

Hi Michael / AtlasCare team,

Thanks again for a productive Q4 — really appreciate the collaborative approach you've taken during the proof-of-concept. As we approach the contract renewal, I wanted to put a concrete proposal on the table to cover the support and SLO commitments your team requested. Key points in this package: 

- Term: 12 months (renewing Jan 1, 2027) with an option to extend to 24 months at a price-protected rate.
- Support: move from Standard to Premium Support (24x7 response for Sev1, named CSM, quarterly architectural reviews).
- Latency SLOs (addendum): target p50/p95 for production inference in us-east: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms on the primary model under the agreed request profile.
- Capacity: reserved dedicated pool sized for your expected baseline throughput (details in attached SOW).
- Pricing: uplift of ~18% for the Premium + dedicated capacity; we can provide a phase-in if you want to ramp.

I've attached the updated SOW (AtlasCare_SOW_v3.pdf) and a draft SLA addendum (redwood-premium-sla-addendum.docx) that translates the technical SLOs into contractual language. If these numbers look reasonable, can we set a 30-minute call next week to walk through the SLA language and the DocuSign flow?

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the latency SLOs & region requirement.
2) Procurement to confirm PO/terms.
3) Sign addendum and SOW via DocuSign, target signature by Dec 10 to lock Jan 1 start.

Open to trade-offs (e.g., slightly looser p95 in exchange for a lower uplift, or a dedicated pool vs. multi-tenant with fallback). Let me know what matters most for your team.

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: AtlasCare_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf))
(attachment: redwood-premium-sla-addendum.docx (docx))

From: Michael Tan <mtan@atlascare.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@atlascare.io>, Evelyn Murphy <evelyn.murphy@atlascare.io>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — Support tier uplift & SLO addendum for AtlasCare

Thanks Priyom — big thanks to you and the team. A few clarifying questions before we schedule the call:

- Can you clarify the test profile for the p95 number? Our traffic has bursts tied to nightly batch jobs and some calendar-driven spikes.
- Is the p95 measured per request across CPU/GPU nodes or at the edge (overall time to first token)? We need guarantees around 95th percentile tail under sustained bursts.
- For region: we require primary inference in us-east with failover to eu-west. Does the addendum support regionally pinned SLOs?

Procurement (cc'd) will want the final DocuSign bundle and an estimate of early termination/credits if SLOs are missed in the ramp window. Evelyn is our purchasing lead and will coordinate PO and legal.

If you can reply with those clarifications I can loop in Legal for redlines. Otherwise happy to take the 30-minute call.

Thanks,
Michael
VP Engineering, AtlasCare

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Michael Tan <mtan@atlascare.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@atlascare.io>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — Support tier uplift & SLO addendum for AtlasCare

Hi Michael — thanks, good questions. Short answers and options below.

- Test profile / p95: the SLO numbers in the addendum are measured at the Redwood ingress (time-to-first-token) over production traffic. For your expected profile (median request size ~600 tokens, 95th token count < 1,200), we see p50 ~90-110ms and p95 ~300-350ms in us-east on a dedicated pool. For burst scenarios we recommend an autoscaling buffer or a small dedicated burst pool to avoid p95 regressions.

- Measurement point: time-to-first-token at the gateway + model compute time is how we measure. We can include a clause that clarifies measurement at the public API endpoint with tags for region.

- Regional SLOs: yes — we can pin the primary SLO to us-east and a separate, lower SLA for eu-west failover (p95 target will be higher on failover). I've added wording in redwood-premium-sla-addendum.docx to reflect both primary and failover SLOs.

- Ramp credits / missed SLOs: proposed credit schedule included in the addendum (scaled credits in month 1-3 during ramp, then standard credits thereafter). We'll have Rishi and our legal operations finalize language.

I've updated the addendum with exact measurement points and a short appendix describing the test profile. Can we do Wednesday Dec 8 at 10am ET / 7am PT for a 30-min call to align with Procurement and Legal?

--

> - For region: we require primary inference in us-east with failover to eu-west. Does the addendum support regionally pinned SLOs?

Best,
Michael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Tan <mtan@atlascare.io>, Procurement <procure@atlascare.io>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: operational note for AtlasCare renewal (pricing & capacity)

Internal note — looping in here so Priyom has the operational context for the call.

- Capacity: AtlasCare wants a guaranteed baseline of 120 QPS during business hours with burst to 600 QPS for calendar peaks. We'll assign a 3-GPU dedicated pool initially (A100-equivalent) and enable an autoscale buffer of +50% for bursts.
- Pricing impact: moving to Premium + dedicated pool + regional failover = estimated ARR uplift of 22% vs current. For a two-year commit we can discount 8%.
- Onboarding: propose a 6-week validation window post-signature; during that period the credit ladder for missed SLOs is more conservative (as Priyom noted).
- Legal: Rishi, please review the addendum wording around regionally pinned SLOs and the measurement appendix before the call.

Priyom — I drafted a short agenda for Wed Dec 8 call and added the HubSpot link in the Doc (HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567890).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
(Internal only message)

From: Michael Tan <mtan@atlascare.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Murphy <evelyn.murphy@atlascare.io>, Procurement <procure@atlascare.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Dec 2026 09:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — Support tier uplift & SLO addendum for AtlasCare

Thanks — we've reviewed the updated addendum and the SOW. Quick confirmation and next steps: 

- AtlasCare accepts the regional primary SLO in us-east and the proposed failover behavior to eu-west.
- We'll sign the addendum and SOW via DocuSign; procurement is preparing the PO (Evelyn cc'd).
- Start date: please target Jan 1, 2027 for the new support tier and dedicated pool.
- One ask: given the ramp risk tied to our calendar spikes, can Redwood provide a 10% credit on month 1 if p95 exceeds the addendum threshold during onboarding? We consider this a one-time ramp protection credit.

If you can confirm the ramp credit and send the DocuSign envelope we can get signatures by Dec 10.

Best,
Michael Tan
VP Engineering, AtlasCare
